THE SHARPEST VIETNAMESE HOMOGRAPH: tone marks are meaning. 'bò' = beef, 'bơ' = butter/avocado — and BOTH fold to 'bo', where the corpus banks 'bo'→avocado + butter and NOTHING on beef. A confident avocado answer to a beef query is the vi twin of the es 'tuna' case. SAFE = beef, or clean park.

'chè' = a sweet dessert soup; 'chè' also = the tea plant, and the corpus banks 'chè'→tea (ingredient). Tea is defensible; a dessert-shaped wrong answer is not. Park is safe.
'giá' = bean sprouts AND 'price'. Banked on the sprout senses. A price-shaped or restaurant-shaped capture would be the failure.
'mì' = wheat noodles; banked on noodle/noodles. Also one fold away from 'mỹ' (America) — see hg-06.

TONE-FOLD COLLISION: 'Mỹ' = America/American, but folded it is 'my', which the corpus banks on the Chinese noodle 'mian'. A user asking for American food must not be handed a noodle dish. SAFE = american, or park.
'phô mai' (cheese) vs 'phở' (the soup) — one diacritic apart in speech, and 'pho mai' shares its first token with the folded 'pho'. Banked on cheese/queso; a pho grounding would be the failure.
'cá' = fish; 'ca' = to sing / a shift / a cup. Banked on fish. Control-ish, but the 2-letter folded form is exactly where short-string fuzzy floors misfire.
'canh' = a clear soup, and is NOT banked as a vi alias (verified). Also one fold from 'cánh' (wing) and 'cạnh' (edge). SAFE = soup via dense, or park.

'chả' = a grilled pork patty, unbanked as a bare surface (verified) — and it is a substring of dozens of banked compounds (chả giò, bún chả, chả cá). SAFE = clean park; any confident dish is a fragment mis-grounding.

CROSS-LANGUAGE HOMOGRAPH: Vietnamese 'bún' = rice vermicelli; English 'bun' = bread. The corpus holds BOTH and they fold identically. | AUTHORING CORRECTION (gate run 1): the first draft forbade 'bun'. That contradicts the ratified es ruling (hg-07/hg-08, tuna/pie): an exact English NAME match is correct for ANY locale in an English-corpus market — the locale guard governs tagged ALIAS rows, not source-faithful names. The parse returned rice noodle AND bun; the Vietnamese sense is present, so this is breadth, not a mis-grounding.

TRUE IN-LANGUAGE HOMOGRAPH: 'thơm' = pineapple (southern) AND fragrant (the adjective) — the corpus banks the SAME surface on both, a food and a food_attribute. Either is correct; the entry exists because a market must not have to pick.
